mainEntity.name: How do I calculate the price before HST in Ontario?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ontario's HST rate is 13%. Divide the HST-inclusive total by 1.13 to find the pre-tax price. Example: $226.00 / 1.13 = $200.00. The HST paid was $26.00.

mainEntity.name: How do I remove GST from a price in Alberta?

acceptedAnswer.text: Alberta charges only the federal 5% GST with no provincial sales tax. Divide your total by 1.05. Example: $105.00 / 1.05 = $100.00 pre-tax price.

mainEntity.name: What is the combined tax rate in Quebec?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quebec charges the 5% federal GST plus the 9.975% QST (Quebec Sales Tax) administered by Revenu Québec. Since 2013, QST is calculated directly on the selling price (not stacked on top of GST), creating a flat combined rate of 14.975%. Divide tax-inclusive receipts by 1.14975 to extract pre-tax amounts.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between GST, HST, and PST in Canada?

acceptedAnswer.text: GST (Goods and Services Tax) is the federal Canadian tax at 5%, applicable in all provinces. HST (Harmonized Sales Tax) combines the federal GST with a provincial component into a single rate, used in Ontario (13%), New Brunswick (15%), Nova Scotia (15%), Newfoundland (15%), and PEI (15%). PST (Provincial Sales Tax) is a separate provincial tax charged alongside GST in British Columbia (7%), Saskatchewan (6%), and Manitoba (7%).

mainEntity.name: How do I reverse calculate GST/HST for an input tax credit claim?

acceptedAnswer.text: To claim an input tax credit (ITC) from the Canada Revenue Agency, you need the GST/HST component of a purchase. Use the reverse formula to find the pre-tax price, then subtract it from the total to get the exact tax paid. Example for Ontario HST: Total $565.00 / 1.13 = $500.00 pre-tax. HST component = $65.00. This $65.00 is your claimable ITC.

mainEntity.name: Which Canadian provinces have the highest combined sales tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Atlantic provinces have the highest combined rates. Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, and Prince Edward Island all have a 15% HST. Ontario's 13% HST is mid-range. Alberta remains the lowest with only the 5% federal GST and no provincial sales tax.

mainEntity.name: What is the reverse VAT formula?

acceptedAnswer.text: The reverse VAT formula is identical to reverse sales tax: Net Price = Gross Price divided by (1 + VAT Rate / 100). For UK 20% VAT: Net = Gross / 1.20. For Germany 19%: Net = Gross / 1.19.

mainEntity.name: What are the standard VAT rates in the EU?

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate the ex-VAT price from a gross amount?

acceptedAnswer.text: Divide the gross VAT-inclusive amount by 1 plus the decimal VAT rate. For 20% VAT: divide by 1.20. For 19% VAT: divide by 1.19. For 10% VAT (Australia GST): divide by 1.10. The result is the net ex-VAT price.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between VAT and US sales tax for reverse calculations?

mainEntity.name: What is the formula for reverse sales tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: The reverse sales tax formula is: Original Price = Final Price divided by (1 + Tax Rate / 100). For example, if you paid $107.50 at a 7.5% tax rate: $107.50 / 1.075 = $100.00 pre-tax price.

mainEntity.name: Why do you divide instead of subtract the tax percentage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because sales tax is applied to the pre-tax price, not the final total. Division is the exact mathematical inverse of the original multiplication. mainEntity.name: What is the sales tax rate in Arizona?

acceptedAnswer.text: Arizona does not have a traditional retail sales tax; instead, it levies a Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT) on businesses for the privilege of operating in the state. The statutory state base TPT rate is 5.60%. However, Arizona counties add excise taxes (0.28% to 1.30%) and incorporated cities levy municipal privilege taxes (1.50% to 2.90%). In major cities like Phoenix (8.60%), Tucson (8.70%), and Mesa (8.30%), the combined TPT rate typically ranges between 7.80% and 9.20%.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate reverse sales tax from an Arizona receipt?

acceptedAnswer.text: To calculate the pre-tax price from an Arizona receipt, divide the total amount paid by 1 plus the combined TPT rate as a decimal (1 + Rate / 100). For example, in Phoenix with an 8.60% combined rate, divide a $108.60 receipt total by 1.086 to determine the original pre-tax price of $100.00. The TPT amount passed to the buyer is $8.60.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Arizona TPT and standard sales tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard retail sales tax is a direct tax on the consumer collected by the vendor as a fiduciary. Arizona's Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT) is an excise tax legally imposed on the vendor for the privilege of conducting business in Arizona (A.R.S. Title 42, Chapter 5). Although businesses are legally authorized to pass the tax cost along to customers on receipts, the vendor remains strictly liable to the Arizona Department of Revenue (ADOR) for remitting the tax.

mainEntity.name: Does Arizona permit tax-inclusive pricing ("factoring")?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The Arizona Department of Revenue (ADOR) explicitly allows businesses to include TPT in the marked sales price, commonly known as "factoring." Under ADOR rules and Form TPT-2 filing instructions, vendors back out the tax by dividing total gross collections by 1 + the combined tax rate to report taxable gross receipts and calculate tax liability.

mainEntity.name: Are groceries and prescription drugs exempt from Arizona sales tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under Arizona Revised Statutes § 42-5102, unprepared food products intended for home consumption (groceries) and prescription medications are exempt from the state 5.60% TPT and county excise taxes. However, Arizona cities have statutory authority under the Model City Tax Code to tax retail food for home consumption; some municipalities levy a 1% to 2.5% local tax on groceries, while others grant a full exemption.

mainEntity.name: How do businesses report factored sales on Arizona Form TPT-2?

acceptedAnswer.text: Businesses registered with ADOR file their Transaction Privilege Tax returns online via AZTaxes.gov. On Form TPT-2, vendors record gross receipts. If prices include TPT, the business uses the reverse calculation formula (Total ÷ (1 + Combined Rate)) to separate gross receipts from TPT collections, enters the factored gross amount on Schedule A, and claims any statutory exemptions on Schedule B.

mainEntity.name: What is the TPT rate for prime contracting in Arizona?

acceptedAnswer.text: Prime contracting in Arizona (construction, remodeling, repairs) has a unique TPT tax base under A.R.S. § 42-5075. Contractors are taxed on 65% of the total contract price (a statutory 35% standard deduction representing materials and non-labor costs), multiplied by the applicable state, county, and municipal tax rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the highest and lowest combined tax rates in Arizona?

acceptedAnswer.text: The highest combined rates in Arizona reach 10.60% to 11.20% in certain smaller municipalities and resort areas with dedicated hospitality taxes (such as Sedona or select mining towns with overlapping special district levies). The lowest combined rates occur in unincorporated rural county areas without municipal additions, where only the 5.60% state rate and minimal county excise tax apply (typically 6.10% to 6.60%).

mainEntity.name: What is the sales tax rate in California in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of 2026, California has a mandatory statewide base sales tax rate of 7.25%, consisting of a 6.00% state general levy and a 1.25% mandatory Bradley-Burns local allocation. When local voter-approved district taxes (Transactions and Use Taxes) are added, actual checkout sales tax rates across California range from 7.25% to 10.75% depending on the specific city and county.

mainEntity.name: How do you calculate sales tax backwards from a California receipt?

mainEntity.name: Why is California sales tax different in every city?

acceptedAnswer.text: While California enforces a statewide base rate of 7.25%, local voters can approve special Transactions and Use Taxes (district taxes) to fund municipal services, transit systems, parks, and libraries. These local add-ons range from 0.10% to over 3.50%, creating differing combined rates across California's 482 cities.

mainEntity.name: What is the highest sales tax rate in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: The highest combined sales tax rate in California is 10.75%, levied in Alameda County municipalities including Alameda, Albany, Newark, San Leandro, and Union City. In these jurisdictions, voter-approved transportation, healthcare, and civic district taxes add 3.50% on top of the 7.25% state base.

mainEntity.name: What is the lowest sales tax rate in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lowest sales tax rate in California is 7.25%, which is the mandatory statewide base rate. This rate applies in rural jurisdictions that have enacted zero local district taxes, including Alpine County, Modoc County, Sierra County, and unincorporated areas of Calaveras, Inyo, and Shasta counties.

mainEntity.name: Are groceries and food taxable in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under CDTFA Regulation 1602, cold, unprepared grocery food staples (produce, dairy, bakery bread, raw meat) sold for home consumption are exempt from sales tax. However, hot prepared food, restaurant dine-in meals, carbonated beverages, alcohol, and food sold under the 80/80 rule (Regulation 1603) are fully taxable.

mainEntity.name: How does the 80/80 rule work in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under CDTFA Regulation 1603, if a food vendor derives more than 80% of its revenue from food sales and more than 80% of those food sales are taxable (e.g., hot food or dine-in meals), all food sales—including cold takeaway items—become subject to sales tax unless the seller maintains detailed, segregated cash register accounting records.

mainEntity.name: How is sales tax calculated on a car purchase in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under CDTFA Regulation 1610, vehicle sales tax is calculated based on the buyer's home registration address where the car is registered with the DMV, not where the dealership is located. Furthermore, California does NOT allow trade-in vehicle values to reduce the taxable sales price; sales tax is paid on the full purchase price.

mainEntity.name: Are trade-ins deducted from sales tax on vehicle purchases in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. California Revenue and Taxation Code explicitly prohibits deducting vehicle trade-in allowances from the taxable gross receipt. If you purchase a vehicle for $35,000 and receive a $10,000 trade-in credit for your used vehicle, California sales tax is assessed on the full $35,000 purchase price.

mainEntity.name: Is software-as-a-service (SaaS) and digital software taxable in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under CDTFA Regulation 1502, pure SaaS accessed remotely via cloud servers is exempt from California sales tax because no tangible personal property is transferred. Electronically downloaded software and digital goods (e-books, digital music) are also exempt. However, canned software delivered on physical media (USB, DVD) is fully taxable.

mainEntity.name: Are digital goods, streaming media, and e-books taxable in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Under California Revenue and Taxation Code Section 6016, sales tax applies solely to tangible personal property that can be seen, weighed, measured, or touched. Electronically delivered digital media, streaming movies, digital photos, podcasts, and e-books are completely exempt from California sales and use tax.

mainEntity.name: Are shipping and freight charges taxable in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under CDTFA Regulation 1628, shipping charges are exempt if items are shipped directly to the customer via common carrier (USPS, FedEx, UPS) and actual delivery costs are stated separately on the invoice. Handling and processing charges are always taxable. If shipping and handling are combined into a single fee, the handling portion is taxable.

mainEntity.name: What is California Use Tax and who is required to pay it?

acceptedAnswer.text: California Use Tax is a companion tax to sales tax imposed at the identical rate on taxable goods purchased without sales tax from out-of-state or online retailers for use, storage, or consumption in California. California residents must declare and remit unpaid use tax on their annual California state tax return (FTB Form 540) or directly to the CDTFA.

mainEntity.name: What are the California economic nexus rules for out-of-state sellers under AB 147?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under California Assembly Bill 147, an out-of-state remote seller is required to register with the CDTFA and collect California sales tax if their total sales of tangible personal property delivered into California exceed $500,000 in the preceding or current calendar year. California has no 200-transaction threshold test.

mainEntity.name: Can a California business include sales tax in displayed prices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Under CDTFA Regulation 1700, retailers may include sales tax in marked prices (common in bars, food trucks, and festivals) provided they post a visible sign stating: 'All prices include California sales tax reimbursement,' or state 'Tax Included' on menus and receipts. When filing taxes, they back out the sales tax using the reverse formula.

mainEntity.name: What is the sales tax rate in Florida?

acceptedAnswer.text: Florida has a statewide base sales tax rate of 6.00%. In addition, counties may levy a local discretionary sales surtax ranging from 0.50% to 1.50%. This makes the combined sales tax rate 7.00% in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach, 7.50% in Hillsborough (Tampa) and Duval (Jacksonville), and 6.50% in Orange County (Orlando). The statewide weighted average rate is approximately 7.13%.

mainEntity.name: What is the Florida $5,000 discretionary sales surtax cap?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under Florida Statute Section 212.054(2)(b), the county discretionary sales surtax applies only to the first $5,000 of the purchase price on any single item of tangible personal property. The state 6.00% rate applies to the full purchase price. For example, on a $10,000 boat or vehicle in a 7% county, the full $10,000 pays 6% ($600), while only the first $5,000 pays the 1% county surtax ($50), totaling $650 in tax (effective 6.50% rate) rather than $700.

mainEntity.name: How do I calculate reverse sales tax from a Florida receipt?

acceptedAnswer.text: To calculate the pre-tax price from a Florida receipt under $5,000, convert your county combined rate into a decimal divisor (1 + Rate / 100) and divide the final receipt total. For a 7.00% receipt in Miami, divide the total by 1.070 (e.g., $107.00 ÷ 1.07 = $100.00 pre-tax). For single items exceeding $5,000, subtract the capped county tax ($5,000 × County Surtax) and divide the remainder by 1.06.
